newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-TRACY LOOKING FOR FOURTH STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TRACY LOOKING FOR FOURTH STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Canadian Paul Tracy, the hottest driver in the CART Indy Car series, scorched the one-mile Milwaukee Oval on Saturday to win the pole for Sunday's Miller 200 in record time.
Looking for his fourth straight win, Tracy claimed the pole in his Penske Mercedes-Benz with a record lap of 20.160 seconds at an average speed of 184.286 mph (296.571 kph).
Tracy smashed the previous track record set by Brazil's Raul Boesel, last week's pole winner at St. Louis, by more than 1.5 seconds.
Mauricio Gugelmin of Brazil was second fastest at 20.385 in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz. Boesel, driving a Reynard Ford, was third fastest in 20.434 seconds.
Even though Tracy was third fastest in unofficial practice his Penske crew decided to make a change in his car overnight.

"We got a little side-tracked yesterday in terms of setup... we've only got about 40 minutes running with this setup," Tracy explained. "There's still more there (in the car), but this was the best lap we've done all weekend."
One of the most aggressive drivers in the series, Tracy didn't seem too concerned about extending his winning streak and tying a mark set by his teammate, Al Unser, Jr.
"I haven't thought about it," Tracy said after winning his second pole of the season. "It would be nice to tie a record. But what's important is the championship."
If Tracy should win on Sunday it would be the 100th win in the series for team owner Roger Penske.
Meanwhile Gugelmin and Boesel, a former World Sports Car Champion, are both looking for their first win in the series.
Boesel said: "Paul is on a high he's had an incredible last three races. We have to be consistent and have great pit-stop strategy for the race."
Patrick Carpentier, fastest in Friday's unofficial practice, was fourth fastest in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Twenty-seven drivers will start Sunday's 200-mile (321 km) race, the seventh in the 17-race series.
